title: GOAT Listing Failure Rate
dataSources: StockX market prices (`stockx:price`), GOAT listings (`goat:listing`), Alias sales (`alias:sale`), sneaker rotation logs (`sneaker:rotation`), and deadstock age checks (`deadstock:age`).
app: StockX price alerts, GOAT listing exports, Alias seller settlement logs, sneaker rotation wear trackers, and deadstock age audits ingested into Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=goat:listing
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(listing_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by sku
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often GOAT listing records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each SKU.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize listing_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per SKU.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights which parts of your GOAT listing data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
